Good to Know
Getting-Ready Room Rules

All beverages in the getting-ready rooms must be ordered through BABC — no outside drinks. No hard alcohol. Water is set up; champagne, wine, beer, or soft drinks can be pre-ordered. Bring your own snacks and food — BABC does not supply food in getting-ready rooms.

Your Florals

Venus has ordered and will have all the bridesmaid bouquets and her own bridal bouquet ready to go on the day — no action needed from you. The florals on the arch and floral meadow along the aisle will be flipped to table centerpieces after the ceremony (see Floral Flip below).

Floral Flip — We Need Your Help! 🌸

After the ceremony, the groomsmen do the heavy lifting — moving floral pieces from the Lawn/Ceremony space to their dinner table positions inside. Desiree leads the flip. Your job is to make sure things land in the right spot and look beautiful once placed. Mostest is not on-site during this window — they set up in the morning and return at the end of the night for breakdown. Here's what moves where:

Item Qty Ceremony Location → Moves to Dinner
Meadow 4 Front line (2 per side) Tables 1, 2, 5 & 6
Short Stand + Large Centerpiece 2 Front line (1 per side, outer) In front of DJ booth
Tall Stand + Grand Centerpiece 2 Front line (1 per side, inner) North & south ends of DJ booth
Floral Swag 2 End of aisle, inside chair Head Table

Desiree leads. Groomsmen carry. Bridesmaids make sure it looks right. Mostest is not on-site — this is the wedding party's show during cocktail hour (5:00–6:00 pm) while guests are on the Patio. Tables 3, 4, 7, 8, and the remaining Head Table pieces are vaseless centerpieces ordered separately — nothing to flip there.

End of Night

After party at Tiny's Hi-Dive, Santa Monica — 2am closing, walk-in. A shuttle from BABC is confirmed (GTS Charter, 40-passenger — see Vendors tab). Please help Venus collect any personal items at the end of the event — designate someone to sign off on cards and gifts from the wedding closet.

Your Role on the Day
💌

Each bridesmaid has a special role on the wedding day. These aren't just titles — they're how we make sure Venus has the most magical, stress-free day possible. Own it!

Alexandra Lisi-Eiselen · Venus Watch Duty
👀 "Does she look perfect?"

Alexandra is Venus's eyes and mirror all day. This means: checking for food in teeth before photos, making sure the dress is properly bustled after the ceremony, smoothing the veil, catching any lipstick moments, and giving a quiet thumbs-up (or a gentle intervention) whenever something's off. If Venus looks anything less than flawless in a photo, it's Alexandra's job to notice first.

Willa Smith · Venus Eats Duty
🍽️ "Has she eaten anything?"

Willa is Venus's personal food coordinator. This starts while getting ready — make sure Venus actually eats something before the ceremony. During cocktail hour, Willa is grabbing hors d'oeuvres and getting them into Venus's hands. At dinner, Willa is watching to make sure Venus gets to eat her actual meal and isn't just chatting the whole time. Hydration counts too.

Emily Arroyo & Shoma Nath · Wrangler Duty
📋 "Is everyone where they need to be?"

Emily and Shoma are the operation leads. They're the first line of defense for any question Desiree, the venue, or any vendor has on the day — so Venus and Matthew don't have to be pulled away from their moment. This means: keeping the wedding party on schedule, helping the groomsmen stay on track with timing, making sure everyone's lined up when they need to be, and fielding any logistical curveballs with a smile.

Isabelle Mollicone · Vibes Duty
🎶 "Is the energy right?"

Isabelle is the vibe curator and energy keeper. Getting ready: great playlists, good energy, everyone's having fun. Cocktail hour: making sure every bridesmaid has a drink in hand and is actually enjoying the moment. Throughout the night: keeping the mood up, getting people on the dance floor, and making sure the whole crew is celebrating as hard as the couple.

Your Role on the Day
💌

Every groomsman has a specific role on the day. These keep Matthew and Venus free to be fully present while the people around them handle the details. Own it!

Kai McNamee · Officiant
💍 "I now pronounce you..."

Kai is running the ceremony — the most important 30 minutes of the day. Walk to the altar first, get positioned, and hold the space while everyone else processes in. After the ceremony, Kai signs the marriage license as officiant and makes sure it's returned to the county within 10 days. The whole thing is in Kai's hands — no pressure 😄

Marriage License — Action Required After the Wedding 📋

As officiant, Kai is legally responsible for signing and returning the marriage license. Venus and Matthew will obtain their license from Beverly Hills Courthouse before the wedding.

1
Sign the license at the ceremony
After Venus and Matthew exchange vows, Kai signs the marriage license as officiant. The two witnesses also sign — planned witnesses are Annie Morawiec and Justin Law. All signatures must be completed on the day of the wedding. Do not leave the venue without signing.
2
Return within 10 days
California law requires the signed license to be returned to the issuing county clerk within 10 days of the ceremony. The wedding is Nov 10 — so the hard deadline is November 20, 2026. Do not wait on this.
3
Option A — Return in person (recommended)
Drop off the signed license at the Beverly Hills Courthouse, 9355 Burton Way, Beverly Hills, CA 90210. Hours: Mon–Fri 8:30 am – 4:30 pm. No appointment needed for drop-off. This is the fastest way to confirm receipt and get immediate proof that it has been filed.
4
Option B — Mail it
Mail the signed license to:
Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk
Marriage Licenses, P.O. Box 1208, Norwalk, CA 90651-1208

If mailing, use a trackable service (USPS Certified Mail or Priority Mail) and mail immediately after the wedding — no later than Nov 12 — to ensure it arrives within the 10-day window. Keep the tracking receipt as proof of timely submission.

⚠️ Important: Do not alter, white-out, or use correction fluid anywhere on the license — any errors must be corrected by the county clerk and cannot be fixed by the officiant. Keep the license flat, dry, and in a safe place until it is returned. The signed license is what legally makes Venus and Matthew married, so guard it carefully on the night!

Justin Law · Family Wrangler
📸 "Everyone needs to be over here, now."

Justin is the human coordinator for all family and wedding party moments. This means: making sure everyone is in the right spot for photos when the photographer is ready, giving people a heads-up before speeches so they're not mid-conversation when the mic goes live, ensuring parents and key family members are on the floor for the Father-Daughter and Mother-Son dances, and generally keeping the family side moving smoothly so Desiree doesn't have to chase people down.

Jonathan Rich · Gear Check
👔 "Did you bring your tie?"

Jon makes sure Matt and the rest of the groomsmen actually have everything they need for the day — ties, cufflinks, shoes, socks, and any other small pieces of the outfit that are easy to forget. Send out reminders ahead of time and do a quick visual check once everyone's getting ready, so nobody's realizing they left something at home when it's too late to fix it.

Xander Lee · Vibes Duty
🎶 "Is the energy right?"

Xander keeps the energy up on the groom's side all day — good music and good vibes while getting ready, making sure the guys are having fun (not just standing around waiting), and getting the crew fired up and ready to celebrate once the ceremony's done.

Thomas Li · Time Manager
⏱ "We need to leave in 10 minutes."

Thomas is the group's clock. Getting ready: making sure the groomsmen are actually ready on time and not dragging their feet. Getting to the venue: keeping everyone on schedule so no one's rushing at the last minute. Throughout the day: aware of what's coming next on the timeline and giving the crew a quiet heads-up before each key moment so nothing catches anyone off guard. Thomas is also on beer pong table duty — see the note below.

Beer Pong — Setup & Breakdown

Justin and Liz can set up beer pong whenever they arrive at the venue — early, before the ceremony, is totally fine. The table can be left out for the rest of the night. All the groomsmen help break it down toward the end of the night. Thomas makes sure the table actually gets put back in Venus's car before the night ends — easy to forget once the after-party shuttle is loading up, so it's on him to close the loop.

For Desiree — Items We're Bringing to BABC
Setup, Display & End-of-Night Collection

Full list of items Venus & Matthew are bringing to the venue, with what needs to happen at setup and at the end of the night. Everything Desiree collects can be loaded straight into Venus's Tesla.

1
Bag of Merch
XL t-shirts, baseball hats, bucket hats. Location: entryway table of the lounge. Guests take what they want throughout the night — collect any leftovers at the end.
2
Welcome Sign
Mirror on a metal stand. Location: base of the stairs leading to the ceremony area. Needs simple assembly — all tools included. Collect after the wedding.
3
Floor-Standing Mirror (Escort Keychains)
Location: courtyard, against the wall closest to the Dining Room, next to the Seating Chart Mirror and one Vinyl Standing Poster — see the floor plan reference image on the Reception tab for exact placement. Escort keychains need to be hung onto this mirror once it's set up at BABC. Collect the mirror after the wedding — keychains themselves go home with guests (see item 7).
4
Seating Chart Mirror
Mirror with the full seating chart — names for all tables. Location: courtyard, against the wall closest to the Dining Room, next to the Floor-Standing Mirror and one Vinyl Standing Poster — see the floor plan reference image on the Reception tab for exact placement. Same metal stand as the Welcome Sign, simple assembly. Collect after the wedding.
5
3x Vinyl Standing Posters
Locations: 1x in the courtyard with the Floor-Standing Mirror and Seating Chart Mirror (see floor plan reference on the Reception tab); 2x next to each bar (one per bar). Come with stands that need simple assembly. Toss after the wedding — no need to collect.
6
Bag of Table Numbers
Framed table numbers, one bag. Location: one framed number per table, placed according to the Reception tab's table layout. Head Table does not get a frame. Collect after the wedding.
7
Escort Keychains
Ping-pong ball + tassel keychains, hung on the floor-standing mirror (item 3, courtyard) at setup. Guests take these home — nothing to collect.
8
Place Cards
Names and entrée selection printed on each card, sorted by table into little baggies. Location: placed directly at each guest's seat at the table in the Dining Room — guests do not pick these up separately. Toss after the wedding — no need to collect.
9
2x Linen Bar Signs
Both signs are identical — location: can go on either bar. Toss after the wedding — no need to collect, both can go.
10
2x Signature Drink Signs (Framed)
Location: one per bar, alongside the linen bar signs. Collect after the wedding — framed, not disposable like the linen signs.
11
Folding Beer Pong Table + Tablecloth
Location: see the floor plan reference image on the Reception tab for exact setup spot. Set up for cocktail hour, collapsed at 10:00 pm. Justin (brother of the bride) oversees this — setup and breakdown. Table: collect after the wedding. Tablecloth: toss after the wedding.

How the Service Works
Directional service — 1 director. Guests self-park; director welcomes/directs guests, assists rideshare at arrival, controls traffic, directs to entrance, and assists rideshare/shuttle at departure. Covers 7 hours (3:00–10:00 pm) + 30 min overtime.
